title: CRASH-081: array filter stale argstack zvalpp across callback uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at ext/standard/array.c:3938 in zif_array_filter when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src e615889d6b43, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/array.c:3938 (also 3903-3905, 3914)
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build crashes on it natively, so a silence on an arm is not a MISSED: under the judge's default scoring the case reads out-of-denominator on every arm; the sensitivity scoring (run-realphp.py --score-oracle-crashes) reads it by fault site instead.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has zif_array_filter at ext/standard/array.c:3938 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the seam present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the allocator seam retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)
